blocks.text: Nouns in the instrumental case decline unusually compared to other cases, using rules that aren't found elsewhere. While not as complex as the genitive plural, it still warrants extra attention.

items: Nouns ending in **о** or a consonant have **-ом** in the instrumental. However, if this ending syllable is both a) unstressed, and b) preceded by the five-letter rule (**ч, ж, ш, щ, ц**), then the ending becomes **-ем**.
карандаш --> карандашом - ends in ш, but ending syllable is stressed
муж - мужем - ends in ж and is unstressed

Nouns ending in **й**, **е**, or **ь**, have the ending **-ем**. If this ending is stressed, it becomes **-ём**. This applies mainly to masculine and neuter nouns; See below for feminine nouns ending in **ь**.
день --> днём - e is a fleeting vowel, so vanishes when the word declines
Those ending in **а** of any gender have **-ой**. As above, if the ending is both unstressed and ends in the five-letter rule, the ending becomes **-ей**.
курица --> курицей - untressed ending and stem ends in ц
груша --> грушей - unstressed ending and stem ends in ш
The ending **я** of any gender becomes **-ей**. If stressed, it becomes **-ёй**.
свинья --> свиньёй - stress on end syllable
Feminine nouns ending in **ь** have **-ью** in the instrumental.

blocks.text: So masculine and neuter nouns have the endings **ом**, **ем**, or **ём**, and feminine nouns have **ой**, **ей**, **ёй**, or **ью**.

There are two general endings for the instrumental plural: **ами** and **ями**. If the noun ends in a consonant, **а**, or **о**, the ending is **ами**. However, if such a noun has an irregular nominative plural that ends in **я**, use **ями** instead. If the noun ends in **й**, **ь**, **я** or **е**, use **ями**. In the following examples, the first word is the nom. sing., the last is the inst. pl., and the middle word (if one is given) is the nom. pl.:

items: брат --> братья --> братьями - note the irregular nominative plural
друг --> друзья --> друзьями - note the irregular nominative plural

blocks.text: There are four words which have the irregular instrumental plural ending **ьми**, but two of them nowadays can also end with **ями** (the four words given are the nom. sing., the nom. pl., and the inst. pl.):

Adjectives modifying masculine or neuter nouns in the instrumental case have two endings: adjectives which have the default ending **ый** or **ое** have the instrumental ending **ым**, and those which end in **ий** or **ее** have **им**. Feminine adjectives have the same endings as the genitive, prepositional, and dative cases: **ой**, or, if the adjective's stem ends in the five letter rule (**ц, ш, щ, ч, ж**) or it has the soft ending (**ний**), the ending is **ей**.
The plural ending is **ыми**. For adjectives that end in **ий**, the ending is **ими**.

items: Она шла в шко́лу с её но́выми друзья́ми
She walked to school with her new friends
Они живу́т ме́жду ста́рыми ру́сскими кни́жными магази́нами
They live between the old Russian bookshops
Sasha was under the pink bed
